Column.ExpandableText: CUI is a component library for C. It draws everything itself, so an app looks the same on Windows, macOS and Linux, and it ships the parts most apps need: inputs, pickers, menus, dialogs, tables, charts and a command palette. Every component supports the keyboard, light and dark themes and reduced motion. The core is plain C99 with no dependencies, and it renders through OpenGL or a built-in software rasterizer, so it also runs in virtual machines and over remote desktop.

Column.ChatMessage: Why do immediate mode toolkits feel so fast? Cite a few sources.

Reasoning.Name: think
Reasoning.Text: The question is about perceived speed. Two parts: how little work a frame does, and how quickly input shows up on screen.
Look for sources on retained versus immediate mode, text rendering cost and motion.

Column.Typewriter: They do very little work per frame: the interface is rebuilt from your data, laid out once and drawn in a handful of batches, so there is no tree of objects to keep in sync. Text is the expensive part, which is why glyphs are cached in an atlas, and motion feels quick when it is driven by springs instead of fixed curves.
